pull.title: refactor: avoid redundant input lookup in `CheckTxInputs`
pull.body:
`Consensus::CheckTxInputs` currently makes two UTXO lookups per input: first through a `HaveInputs()` pre-pass (which internally calls `HaveCoin()` for every input), and then through `AccessCoin()` on the same outpoints in the main validation loop. `HaveInputs()` has only a single caller (`CheckTxInputs`), and `AccessCoin()` already returns a reference to a spent sentinel `Coin` for any missing outpoint. This means the presence check can be folded into the existing loop without changing behavior. This PR removes the initial `HaveInputs()` pre-pass and instead checks `coin.IsSpent()` immediately after `AccessCoin()` returns. As a result, `CheckTxInputs` performs one lookup per input instead of two (2N → N, where N is the number of inputs) in the validation path shared by both `ConnectBlock` and mempool acceptance. `HaveInputs()` itself is **not** removed. It is still used by the coins-view fuzz harness, although this change leaves it with no callers in the validation hot path. Removing it would be a trivial follow-up. The only observable behavioral difference is which validation error is reported if one input is missing while another input in the same transaction fails for some unrelated reason (for example, coinbase immaturity). - In `ConnectBlock`, all such failures are ultimately reported as `BLOCK_CONSENSUS`, so the specific failure reason or ordering has no consensus impact. - In the mempool (`MemPoolAccept::PreChecks`), every input has already been checked with `m_view.HaveCoin()` before `CheckTxInputs()` is called. Missing inputs are handled there as orphan transactions, making the "missing input" path inside `CheckTxInputs()` unreachable during mempool validation.
Benchmark (bench_bitcoin -filter=CheckTxInputs) The benchmark below is intentionally designed to measure the cost of the redundant lookup itself, rather than end-to-end block validation. A fresh `CCoinsViewCache` wrapping `CoinsTip` is constructed for each measured batch (coins are added to `CoinsTip` itself, not to the benchmarked view), so each pass actually crosses the view/base boundary instead of hitting an already-warmed local cache. This closely matches how a fresh per-block view behaves in production. ```bash BEFORE="d31c26fd1a53300a704bccbf12aae5b050c67ec3" AFTER="5021cd02fa503f0ea0dc741f7200eba8275a885d" RESULTS_FILE="$HOME/checktxinputs_bench_results.txt" : > "$RESULTS_FILE" echo "machine | $(hostname) | $(uname -m) | $(lscpu | grep 'Model name' | head -1 | cut -d: -f2 | xargs) | $(nproc) cores | $(free -h | awk '/^Mem:/{print $2}') RAM" | tee -a "$RESULTS_FILE" ORIG="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" for hash in $BEFORE $AFTER; do echo ">>> $hash" git checkout "$hash" >/dev/null 2>&1 && cmake --build build -t bench_bitcoin && ( echo "--- ${hash:0:7} ---" ./build/bin/bench_bitcoin -filter=CheckTxInputs -min-time=3000 ) 2>&1 | tee -a "$RESULTS_FILE" done git switch "$ORIG" ```
| | ns/tx | tx/s | err% | |--------|------:|-----:|-----:| | before | 1,154.31 | 866,316 | 0.4% | | after | 985.84 | 1,014,367 | 0.5% | ~14.6% faster. This is smaller than a naive 2N → N lookup-count argument might suggest, because both lookups are `FetchCoin` calls against the same already-resolved cache entry after the first one resolves it. The second lookup is just a cheap lookup in an already-warm cache, not a second trip to the backing store. The real saving is exactly one redundant cache lookup per input, which is what this benchmark isolates. As a sanity check, I also compared IBD over the same block range before and after this change and observed no measurable difference in synchronization time, which is expected: `CheckTxInputs` accounts for only a small fraction of `ConnectBlock`, where signature verification dominates. The optimization is therefore real but modest. Its value comes from removing a genuinely redundant lookup without changing consensus behavior, rather than from any meaningful IBD speedup. ### Historical context This pre-pass originally served a real purpose. Before April 2017, `CheckTxInputs()` used a per-*txid* `CCoins` cache where `AccessCoins(txid)` returned a raw pointer that could be `NULL`, and a single `CCoins` entry could contain both spent and unspent outputs. In that design, `HaveInputs()` prevented both null-pointer dereferences and spending an already-spent output within an otherwise live entry. On 2017-04-25, two commits changed this: - `0003911326` ("Introduce new per-txout CCoinsViewCache functions") introduced `AccessCoin()`, which returns a reference to a sentinel empty coin for missing outpoints. - `f68cdfe92b` ("Switch from per-tx to per-txout CCoinsViewCache methods in some places") updated `CheckTxInputs()` to use the new API. From that point onward, missing and already-spent outputs were both represented by `coin.IsSpent()` on the object returned by `AccessCoin()`, making the `HaveInputs()` pre-pass redundant. The validation loop has effectively remained unchanged since then, aside from the later scripted rename from `IsPruned()` to `IsSpent()` (`589827975f`). This PR simply removes that leftover redundancy. ~~**Edit:** :When I opened this PR, I hadn't reviewed PR #35187, which modifies the same lines. While the primary goal of that PR is different, it also avoids the redundant lookup as a side effect.~~ ~~Although that PR was submitted earlier, it is significantly larger and includes more critical and potentially controversial changes (it has already received one concept NACK), so it may take longer to be merged.~~ ~~This PR is smaller, focused on a specific issue, and can be evaluated independently. It also doesn't block or conflict with the other PR, since #35187 can still be merged later on top of these changes without any issues.~~ Not anymore

test: cover missing-input outpoint in CheckTxInputs

Exercise the case where a transaction spends an outpoint that is
entirely absent from the coins view. AccessCoin returns a spent
placeholder Coin for it, so it must be rejected the same way as an
already-spent input: bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent.

I'm not necessarily against this change; we've argued this for years now, but as noted in the description, this changes invalid block reason reporting.
Not sure how critical that would be (in https://github.com/l0rinc/bitcoin/pull/137 I deliberately tried avoiding that), but ultimately the effect is small, and after https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35215 it is expected to be even smaller.

Thank you @l0rinc for your comments!!

> we've argued this for years now

Sorry, I wasn't aware,  I tried to do some research before doing the pr but it looks like I missed something.  I am reading the code, profiling and running benchmarks to find things to optimize, but I am not finding that much. I would be glad if you could point me to any issue or problem that has already been discussed but no one is working on :D

> but as noted in the description, this changes invalid block reason reporting.

Personally, I think the impact is minimal. I would say (correct me if I am wrong) the mismatch is only visible locally,  in `debug.log` and in the reject-reason string returned to `submitblock`/`getblocktemplate` proposal callers. It also only happens in the specific scenario where a transaction in a block has a missing input _and_ an earlier input with an unrelated failure. In that case, reporting either of the two reasons seems enough to me. **There is no behavior change in the node's logic**, only which of the two errors is reported changes (one before, another now), so the same amount of information is reported: a single reject reason, just as before.

However im totally open to do any changes or explore a solution to that matter if it is really that relevant!

> looks like I missed something

Not necessarily, some similar discussion happened a long time ago e.g. https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/14837
> the algorithm checks more invariants at once and detects them in a different order than before, clients relying on an exact reject reason may be confused. Clients should already not rely on exact reject reasons, so I don't believe this has a ramification.

> profiling and running benchmarks to find things to optimize, but I am not finding that much

We're working hard to make sure you don't find that much :p
https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35295 may enable new optimizations; you could help by reviewing it.
Just know that consensus refactors are usually ignored if done by [relatively new contributors](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commits?author=arejula27).

> However im totally open to do any changes or explore a solution to that matter if it is really that relevant!

As mentioned, I'm not against it, but I'm personally not prioritizing it (especially while #35295 is still open).

Based on some previous comments about the behavioral change, I ran an  demo on regtest comparing `d31c26f` (BEFORE, without this change) and `5b02e4b` (AFTER, current branch tip) across every RPC channel where a reject reason is observable. For each RPC call I captured both the RPC response and whatever line it produced in `debug.log`.

**Scenarios**

1. **`scenario_both_errors`**: `vin[0]` spends a coinbase with only 1 confirmation (immature), `vin[1]` spends a non-existent outpoint. This is the scenario from the PR description: two unrelated failures in the same tx.
2. **`scenario_missing_first`**: same two failures as (1), but with the missing input ordered first in `vin`.
3. **`scenario_immature_only`**: only the immature-coinbase input (single failure, sanity check).
4. **`scenario_missing_only`**: only the missing outpoint (single failure, sanity check).

**Results**

1. `vin[0]`=immature coinbase, `vin[1]`=missing outpoint (both failures, non-missing first), the scenario from the PR description:

| channel | `d31c26f` (BEFORE) | `5b02e4b` (AFTER) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gbt-proposal` rpc | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | **`bad-txns-premature-spend-of-coinbase`** |
| `gbt-proposal` debug.log | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | **`bad-txns-premature-spend-of-coinbase`** |
| `submitblock` rpc | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | **`bad-txns-premature-spend-of-coinbase`** |
| `submitblock` debug.log | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | **`bad-txns-premature-spend-of-coinbase`** |
| `testmempoolaccept` rpc | `missing-inputs` | `missing-inputs` |
| `testmempoolaccept` debug.log | (none) | (none) |
| `sendrawtransaction` rpc | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` (`-25`) | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` (`-25`) |
| `sendrawtransaction` debug.log | (none) | (none) |


2. `vin[0]`=missing outpoint, `vin[1]`=immature coinbase (order swapped), identical BEFORE/AFTER:

| channel | `d31c26f` (BEFORE) | `5b02e4b` (AFTER) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gbt-proposal` rpc | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` |
| `gbt-proposal` debug.log | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` |
| `submitblock` rpc | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` |
| `submitblock` debug.log | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` |
| `testmempoolaccept` rpc | `missing-inputs` | `missing-inputs` |
| `testmempoolaccept` debug.log | (none) | (none) |
| `sendrawtransaction` rpc | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` (`-25`) | `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` (`-25`) |
| `sendrawtransaction` debug.log | (none) | (none) |

Scenarios 3 and 4 showed the correct/expected error, since each only had a single failure present,  no behavior change in either case.

Note regarding the last "Edit" section of the description: I have checked the current version of #35187 (7bb468db884c885db5af5ab7abc6580b416f650e), and it does not touch this part (file `src/consensus/tx_verify.cpp` in not affected), so I think the information is not valid any more.

@arejula27, please check if this still makes sense now that https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35215 was merged.
And note that we mostly care about mainnet performance, and mostly about the blocks post 7-800k, so only checking it for the first 200k blocks doesn't reveal anything. Also note that a micro-benchmark being a bit faster doesn't usually translate to a real feature getting faster. Given how consensus critical this part is, we likely need a very compelling reason to change it.

> Note that we mostly care about mainnet performance, especially for blocks after height 700-800k.

I will try to re-run the IBD focused on that section of the chain, but it may take a while. My hardware is modest and struggles with the validation, it's an external SSD, and sometimes the chain gets corrupted, so I have to start from zero again.

That said, I don't expect this PR to show impact in that way. Last time, it only showed gains in the micro-benchmarks. So if this PR needs IBD-level impact to be accepted, I'd say there's a high chance it gets dismissed.

> So if this PR needs IBD-level impact to be accepted

Every change is a risk, so we need to be convinced to spend time reviewing this thoroughly to be confident that it's safe to do this. Microbenchmarks are usually enough if the change is trivial otherwise, which arguably isn't the case here.

Yes, I totally understand and make sense, will come back with data 🫡

Btw, found that  `txospenderindex` under-reserves memory: it sizes the vector by tx count, but it actually grows by input count, so it ends up reallocating multiple times per block.
Already got the change implemented, just missing the microbench, worth it to try the PR or is this also critical-path territory?

> Already got the change implemented, just missing the microbench, worth it to try the PR or is this also critical-path territory?

There's one way to find out!

Though note that we're planning on applying the savings from https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35531 there as well (if this one gets in), so a future rewrite is not unlikely.

Closing this.

Re-measured on current master, after #35215 made `CCoinsMap` key hashing cheaper. `bench_bitcoin -filter=CheckTxInputs, -min-time=3000`:

|        | ns/tx  | tx/s      |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| before | 811.51 | 1,232,268 |
| after  | 718.96 | 1,390,892 |

~10.9%, down from the ~14.6% in the description. The saving is one warm-cache lookup per input, never a read from the backing store, and `CheckTxInputs` is a small fraction of `ConnectBlock`: I measured no IBD difference.

Based on the feedback in this thread, I don't think this is worth spending more reviewer time on fr the follwoing reasons: 
- it's a change in consensus-critical code from a new contributor with no merged commits
-  The gain only shows up in the microbenchmark, not in real IBD. 

Thanks for the reviews and your time!!
